transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2027-05-30
- Time: 15:00 UTC / 08:00 PT
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Raman (AxiomGrid Head of Platform), Daniel Hsu (AxiomGrid SRE), Evan Brooks (AxiomGrid Partnerships)

Summary (auto):
Quick partner discovery to map AxiomGrid's hybrid routing needs, understand KV/prefix cache expectations, map Dedicated vs Private options, and plan a baseline perf benchmark. Action items: perf run, security docs, schedule POC.

Topics: hybrid routing, KV cache behavior, batching and latency SLOs, private/VPC deployment considerations, committed capacity pricing, benchmark plan

----- Transcript -----
[00:00] Lena Ortiz: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Lena from Redwood, I'm the AE on this account, with me Marcus Chen our platform SE. How's everyone?
[00:06] Priya Raman: Hey Lena, thanks. Priya here. Morning for us. We pulled in Daniel and Evan. We're excited to chat through integration patterns, we run a hybrid edge-cloud control plane so routing's kinda core for us.
[00:17] Marcus Chen: Great to hear. Curious — can you sketch current traffic patterns? e.g. percent edge vs central, model sizes, 99th token lengths?
[00:26] Daniel Hsu: Sure yeah, rough numbers — 60% of auth-ish inference at the edge (small models, 2–4 tokens avg per request), 40% central for long-form generation, those can be 250–1,200 tokens sometimes. Peak qps around 3k, sustained 700–900.
[00:41] Marcus Chen: Nice, that distribution matters a lot for batching and KV cache strategy. Our runtime does continuous batching but we tune queue windows depending on latency SLOs. For edge we usually recommend smaller batch sizes + aggressive prefix caching.
[00:52] Priya Raman: By prefix caching do you mean the KV cache for previous tokens? We have a lot of repeated prompts (templates) so caching would help.
[00:58] Marcus Chen: Exactly. Redwood supports prefix/KV caching and automatic lookups — but there are tradeoffs: memory on-host vs network hop if using central cache. For your 60% edge pattern, a small local KV cache plus a central warm cache is a common pattern.
[01:12] Evan Brooks: How does that work with private deployments? We're considering Private (on-prem) for some regulated customers. We need KMS and audit logs.
[01:19] Lena Ortiz: Yes we have Redwood Private with a customer-controlled control plane option, integrates with KMS/HSM for keying and produces audit logs (we can send SOC2 and audit spec). Our RBAC and SSO options map to Okta/SAML; we also support per-request metadata for audit.
[01:33] Daniel Hsu: Good. On capacity — is Dedicated easier for predictable throughput? We don't want noisy neighbor stuff for the central cluster.
[01:40] Marcus Chen: Dedicated's the usual answer for predictable throughput. You get reserved GPU pools and we can configure autoscale with burst off a shared pool. For latency-critical, Dedicated + prefix caching + quantization profile is the combo clients pick.
[01:53] Priya Raman: Quantization — do you do int8 for the long-form models we use? We have a custom 7B variant.
[01:58] Marcus Chen: We recommend per-model quantization profiles. Our Optimize tooling can suggest a quant profile — int8 or hybrid quant — and we do kernel selection tuned to the quantized path. There's sometimes a small quality delta; we run evals tied to your prompt set.
[02:10] Priya Raman: Is there an easy way to test quality vs CPU/GPU perf? We need a baseline.
[02:15] Marcus Chen: We can run a perf + quality benchmark. Marcus (SE): we'll do two runs — hosted style (shared) to get cost ballpark, and Dedicated/private sim to measure 95/99 latencies and token throughput. Bring your sample traces.
[02:25] Daniel Hsu: We'll provide the traces. One pain point: our network egress policies are strict. For a Private on-prem deploy, do we need outbound connectivity to Redwood control plane?
[02:34] Lena Ortiz: For Private with customer-managed control plane, minimal outbound for telemetry is optional; there are air-gapped patterns but that increases ops. We'll share the network topology checklist.
[02:45] Evan Brooks: On routing — we need smart routing for cost reason: route to cheaper model variant during non-peak, route to dedicated during business hours. Can Redwood policies support that?
[02:53] Marcus Chen: Yes — policy-based routing by latency, cost, region, customer tier. We can do gradual rollouts, automatic fallback to a cheaper variant when capacity is constrained. We'll want to understand your SLAs and SLOs to set thresholds.
[03:06] Priya Raman: Our SLO targets: p95 sub-250ms for short-form and p95 sub-700ms for long-form generation. Is that realistic?
[03:13] Marcus Chen: For long-form the 700ms p95 is aggressive depending on length; if you stream tokens the initial latency can be lower while total completion time is longer. We can meet those with Dedicated + right batching + KV cache for prefixes.
[03:26] Daniel Hsu: Streaming — do you support chunked token streaming with server side batching? We need to integrate into our edge proxies.
[03:33] Marcus Chen: Yes streaming with chunked tokens and we expose hooks for tracing. We'll provide SDK examples for your proxy. Also talks about streaming/partial responses might change how you measure latency.
[03:43] Priya Raman: Security questions — SOC2, iso27001? We need evidence for enterprise deals.
[03:47] Lena Ortiz: We have SOC2 Type II and ISO docs available. For Private we can map controls to your audit needs. I'll attach the security pack after this call.
[03:55] Evan Brooks: Any competitors we should watch? Our infra team evaluated NimbleServe and CloudFaces for latency. We're comparing TCO.
[04:02] Lena Ortiz: Understood. We can provide a TCO model for hosted vs Dedicated vs Private; often Dedicated hits a sweet spot for predictable TCO and latency.
[04:09] Marcus Chen: Quick note on kernel selection — our runtime selects kernels based on sequence length histograms. If your traces show many long sequences, we'll pick kernels that favor longer context and memory patterns. That impacts CPU/GPU memory and cost.
[04:22] Priya Raman: Nice. For the POC scope — can we run an on-prem POC that uses our edge routing but Redwood's serving runtime in a private VPC? We want to validate routing policy + KV cache effectiveness.
[04:33] Marcus Chen: Yes. Typical POC: 2-3 week window, deploy a private cluster, instrument with your traces, run A/B compare: baseline vs KV-prefetch + quantized variant. We'll measure p50/p95/p99 latency and token cost.
[04:45] Daniel Hsu: We need a checklist for infra and a sample manifest.
[04:48] Lena Ortiz: We'll share the private deployment checklist and a sample helm/k8s manifest. Also a small sample script to seed KV cache from historical prefixes.
[04:56] Evan Brooks: Any gotchas with HSM integration? Our KMS expects strict key rotation.
[05:01] Marcus Chen: We integrate with customer KMS/HSM via standard APIs; rotation policies require a short maintenance window for key exchange but are supported. We'll document the sequence.
[05:09] Priya Raman: What about billing model for Dedicated + burst? We like reserved but want some burst for spiky demand.
[05:15] Lena Ortiz: Reserved monthly commit with configurable burst from shared pool; pricing sheet has example tiers. We'll include burst delta and overage rates in the pricing doc.
[05:24] Daniel Hsu: Perfect. Any immediate blockers from Redwood side to run the perf test?
[05:28] Marcus Chen: We'll need representative traces, a sample config for routing rules, and an account to run the tests. Also a list of model artifacts (weights) or a pointer to the model repo. If you're bringing a custom fork, we'll need the architecture details.
[05:40] Priya Raman: We can share traces and model metadata. We'll need Redwood to sign an IDA before we share internal traces?
[05:45] Lena Ortiz: We can provide our standard NDA/IDA — Marcus will loop in Legal. But we also accept anonymized traces if that moves faster.
[05:53] Evan Brooks: Timeline expectation? We'd like POC by mid-June.
[05:57] Lena Ortiz: Sounds doable. Marcus: are you ok to run the benchmark and we aim for POC kickoff week of June 14?
[06:03] Marcus Chen: Yep I'll run the perf benchmark and share results by June 7, that gives time to prep infra for the June 14 kick.
[06:10] Lena Ortiz: Great. I'll send the pricing and SOC2/security pack today and the deployment checklist. I'll also create a calendar invite for a January... sorry, June 14 POC kickoff tentatively.
[06:20] Priya Raman: Thanks all. One more random question — does Redwood provide tooling to auto-tune batch windows per route?
[06:25] Marcus Chen: Yes our Optimize recommendations include batch window tuning per route and suggestions for cache sizes. We'll surface an expected token-cost delta for each suggestion.
[06:33] Daniel Hsu: Awesome. That answers a lot.
[06:36] Evan Brooks: Ok that's a wrap.
[06:38] Lena Ortiz: Cool — recap and next steps: Marcus runs perf benchmark (due 2027-06-07), Lena shares pricing + SOC2 + checklist (due 2027-05-31), AxiomGrid to share traces and model metadata (due 2027-06-04). We'll tentatively kick POC week of 2027-06-14.
[06:54] (call ends)
